title: byEmployer raises namesake fraud records to 'likely' red flags on employer names that are big companies or ordinary words
scenario: The profile reads earlier employers Square and Google from two tied records. A namesake record 'John Smith charged with fraud in Times Square shooting case' and another 'Former Google engineer John Smith indicted' are both raised to likely and both appear under red flags.
evidence: The temporary buildReport test gave grades likely and likely, and redFlags contained both titles. The employer regex has the 'i' flag and no check that the word is used as a name. Big employers are not excluded.
fix: Make the employer regex case-sensitive and run it through orgMatcher. Exclude employers with a very large headcount (reuse the NOT_PERSON big-company list) or require a second independent anchor. Never raise high or medium severity records by employer alone: list them as namesakes with 'names a former employer' as a hint.
verifyNote: report.js:427 builds the employer regex with the 'i' flag, and the only boundary is alphanumeric. It has no written-as-name or longer-name test, so 'Times Square' matches 'Square'. The only check on serious records is n>=2 tied records, and big employers are not excluded.
betterFix: Use orgMatcher(e.org, subject) in place of the raw regex. Require the employer within the same sentence as the name, and no other affiliation after the name. For high or medium severity, never raise on employer alone: keep the record possible with a hint.

title: ordinaryWordOnly demotes true company records and keeps 'boat ramp' records
scenario: Company typed 'ramp' in lowercase: 'Ramp raises $500M from investors' is demoted to possible, while 'Company fined after crash at boat ramp' stays a company record. Company 'Merge Labs': 'Merge raises $250M in funding' is demoted, because coWord is the literal 'Merge Labs'.
evidence: The temporary buildReport test gave ['Merge Labs','possible'], ['ramp','possible'] and ['ramp boat','company']. STANDS_ALONE is case-sensitive on the typed string and uses the full typed name, not the key.
fix: Build coWord from the key in its proper-cased form ('Ramp', 'Merge') and match it case-sensitively, whatever the user typed. Also accept the full typed name. Run the same written-as-name test as orgMatcher, so the two agree.
verifyNote: coWord comes from the typed state.company and STANDS_ALONE has no 'i' flag. So typed 'ramp' matches 'boat ramp' (which stays company), while 'Ramp raises' gets demoted. 'Merge Labs' as coWord never matches 'Merge raises'.

title: Model-written briefs are never passed through the guardrails
scenario: writeDeepBrief and the quick brief accept the model's text after only citation checks. A model drawing on outside knowledge writes 'Holmes, who has two children and was born in 1984 [Source 3]' with a valid citation. It is shown and saved. The prompt asks the model to leave this out, but code never enforces it.
evidence: report.js check() runs validateAnswer and filters citations only; the founderCheck.js brief path is the same
fix: Post-filter every line of the brief: run redactPII, and drop any line that fails isSensitive, mentionsMinor or the kin rule. Then re-check that citations remain. Apply this in writeDeepBrief, the quick brief and quotedDeepBrief.
verifyNote: report.js check() only re-maps citations. The founderCheck brief only runs validateAnswer. Nothing filters model text for PII or sensitive content. quotedDeepBrief draws on findings that are already sanitized, so it needs the filter less.

title: byEmployer raises name-only records to likely, including a record that says the person is NOT a founder
evidence: buildReport in Jest. With bio 'Shensi Ding previously worked at Expanse', the r8 YC record 'Expanse (founded 2025)… Shensi Ding is not on its founder list' became likely. With the colleague sentence above, a namesake BrokerCheck record at Goldman Sachs also became likely.
scenario: A misread employer (finding 1), or a different company with the same name, turns namesake broker, registry or YC records into 'likely'. The code also matches the person's name inside a title the check wrote itself that denies the tie.
fix: Upgrade only when the source's own text (quote or data.firms, not a title the check wrote) puts the full name and the employer together. Skip records whose text says not listed, not on, or no match. Require the employer to come from 2 or more independent tied records, or from a dated span that overlaps. Feed the dates of an upgraded BrokerCheck record back into the role.
verifyNote: byEmployer tests subject.hasName and the employer regex on title plus quote. It checks no negation ('not on its founder list') and ignores where the title came from. Any employer misread by the pattern path (finding 1) therefore raises namesake possible records to likely, and the gate needs only one supporting record for non-serious records.

title: Degree, field, boards, founded, investments and recognition are hard-coded empty without a model
evidence: reportProfile sets degree:null and field:null, and boards, founded, investments and recognition to []. profile.js never parses degree text, although Wikidata quotes carry 'academic degree …; academic major …'.
scenario: 'She earned a B.S. in Computer Science from Columbia University' shows only 'Columbia University'. 'Forbes 30 Under 30 (2022)' and board seats in tied records never appear when no model runs.
fix: In buildProfile, parse '(B.S.|BA|MBA|Ph.D|bachelor's|master's)[ degree] in <Field> from|at <School>' beside the matched school. Read 'board (member|of directors) of|at X' and 'advis(or|es) X' into boards, 'named to <Forbes 30 Under 30…> (year)' into recognition, and 'angel investor in X' into investments, each guarded as in finding 1. Pass them through reportProfile instead of empty lists.
verifyNote: reportProfile hard-codes degree and field to null and boards, founded, investments and recognition to []. Jest: 'earned a B.A. in Economics from Harvard University' gave only the school. The new extractors must use the finding-1 guard, or they will mis-credit people the same way.

title: A related person is marked 'screened' even when the screen failed
scenario: A relative's sanctions lookup throws because every list failed to load. deepCheck adds the task key to `ran` before running it and keeps it after the error, so it ends up in state.done. The report then shows the relative as screened, against the documented promise to mark any related person not screened in that run.
fix: Keep a separate state.screenedOk list, filled only when a watchlist lookup returns without throwing and without partial. Build `screened` in report.js from that list, not from state.done.
evidence: deepCheck.js:646 runs ran.add(taskKey(task)) before c.run; the catch path does not delete it; line 779 pushes ran into state.done; report.js:636-638 reads done.
verifyNote: deepCheck.js:646 adds the key to ran. The error path (stat.errors++) and the waitedOut path never delete it. Line 779 pushes ran into state.done. report.js:636-638 marks the person screened from done, including offshore-leaks, which never runs for related people.
betterFix: Record per-task outcomes: state.screenedOk keyed by person, added only when a WATCHLISTS lookup resolves with no error and no partial. Mark a person screened only when every watchlist planned for them succeeded. Otherwise show 'screened in part' and name the lists that were missed.

title: Coverage never says Delaware, California and 43 other states' registers were not searched
scenario: A Delaware C-corp with no filings in CO/NY/CT/OR/TX shows 'US state business registers: no match'. A reader takes that as 'not registered'. NY and Oregon list active entities only, so dissolved companies there are invisible too.
fix: Always add a note from us-state-registries naming the states searched, their limits (NY/OR active only, TX franchise taxpayers) and that Delaware and California are not searched. Add to NOT_COVERED: 'Company registers of US states other than CO, NY, CT, OR, TX (including Delaware and California) and of countries other than the UK and France'.
evidence: No 'Delaware' or 'state register' wording in NOT_COVERED. The connector returns no notes when nothing matched.
verifyNote: NOT_COVERED has no entry for other US states or countries, and the connector adds no notes on a no-match result. The source label names the five states searched, which softens it, but Delaware and California are never stated as unsearched, and the active-only limits appear only inside findings.

title: 'Claims that changed' lists other people's bios and marketing-copy edits
scenario: In r9 Glyman, #37 is the bio of 'Stefanie', a content marketer, on a ramp.com blog page. It is graded confirmed and shown as his claim change. #19, #21, #30 and #33 are product-copy and podcast blurb rewrites, as are #4 and #8 in r8 (Shensi Ding). Only #1, #8, #105 and #109 are real claim changes.
fix: Keep a change only when the before or after text names the subject (or opens with a pronoun on the subject's own profile page) and the difference touches a claim token: a title, employer, school, degree or year. Put the other changes in the archive section only, never in claimChanges or the brief.
evidence: r9 claimChanges: n=37 with quote 'Prior to Ramp, Stefanie worked as a finance reporter...', and n=21 with 'Easy-to-use cards, funds, approval flows...'.
verifyNote: report.js line 632 keeps every archive 'change' record that is not 'possible'. archive.js builds bio and headline diffs from whole pages, including company blog pages with several people, and grades a change by the page's match. Nothing checks that the changed text is about the subject. I could not re-check the r9 data myself, but the code allows exactly what the finding describes.
betterFix: Fix this at the source, in archive.js when the change finding is built. For a page that is not the person's own profile, keep a bio or headline change only when its before or after text names the subject. Mark marketing-copy diffs as info and keep them out of claimChanges. The report filter can then also require field in role, title, education or headline, or a bio diff that names the subject.

title: 'Screens with no match' claims clean for screens that waited out, partly answered, or never ran fully
scenario: Sanctions ran 1 lookup and waited out 4; UK Gazette returned partial=['notices']. screensOf marks both 'partial', but cleanScreens lists both under 'Screens with no match' in the brief and in the model's prompt. SCREENS also lacks the delaware-courts, eu-courts, canada-federal-courts, us-bank-regulators, fincen-actions, leak-sites and breach-catalogue ids, so real clean screens go unstated (as in the r9 brief).
fix: Build cleanScreens from screensOf output: status === 'clear' only, with labels from SCREEN_GROUPS and source labels. Delete the separate SCREENS map and the stale 'bodacc' and 'icij' ids. Add waitedOut and partial to coverage.searched rows.
evidence: Jest repro: screens sanctions-lists:partial and uk-gazette:partial, yet cleanScreens returned ['sanctions (US, UN, EU, UK, Canada)','UK Gazette notices'].
verifyNote: Reproduced. screensOf marked sanctions (4 lookups waited out) and uk-gazette (partial) as 'partial', yet cleanScreens returned both as 'Screens with no match', because coverage.searched carries neither waitedOut nor partial. SCREENS also lacks delaware-courts, eu-courts, canada-federal-courts, us-bank-regulators, fincen-actions, leak-sites and breach-catalogue. This breaks rule 5 (honest coverage).

title: Related party shown as 'screened' when its watchlist lookup failed or waited out
scenario: The sanctions lookup for associate Karim Atiyeh fails with HTTP 503. deepCheck still pushes the task key into state.done (failed and waited-out tasks stay in `ran`), and buildReport marks him screened:true. Screens by mdb-debarment, us-bank-regulators and fincen-actions never count, because WATCHLISTS omits them.
fix: In deepCheck, record failed and waited-out task keys (state.failed) and remove them from done, or record succeeded screens explicitly. The report sets screened only from succeeded watchlist tasks and lists the screens that failed for each party. Add mdb-debarment, us-bank-regulators and fincen-actions to WATCHLISTS.
evidence: Jest repro: sources errors=1 of runs=1 and done=['sanctions-lists|associate|Karim Atiyeh|screen'] gave relatedParties[0].screened === true.
verifyNote: Reproduced. A us-exclusions lookup for an associate that failed with HTTP 503 still produced screened:true. In deepCheck.js, failed and waited-out tasks stay in `ran` and go into state.done; only retried or rested tasks are removed. WATCHLISTS also omits mdb-debarment, us-bank-regulators and fincen-actions.
betterFix: In deepCheck, add the task key to state.screenedOk only when a watchlist task returns a result, and keep failed or waited-out keys in state.screenFailed. The report then sets screened from screenedOk and lists the screens that failed for each party. Do not take failed keys out of done, because done also prevents re-queueing.

title: Sanctions, debarment and wanted-list red flags sort below a resignation
scenario: A confirmed high-severity World Bank debarment (category sanctions, source mdb-debarment) and a medium 'Trevor Milton resigns as chairman' press item are both red flags. flagWeight gives the debarment 0, because FLAG_WEIGHTS has no sanction, debar or wanted terms and only 'regulatory' has a fallback. The resignation (1) leads, and severity is never compared.
fix: Give category sanctions weight 5 and regulatory 4 before the title is read. Add bar and sanction events to FLAG_WEIGHTS, and break ties on SEVERITY_WEIGHT before sourceAuthority. Add mdb-debarment, us-bank-regulators, fincen-actions, delaware-courts, eu-courts, canada-federal-courts and us-agency-orders to PRIMARY_SOURCES so the authority's record leads its matter.
evidence: Jest repro: redFlags order was [web-search medium resignation, mdb-debarment high].
verifyNote: Reproduced. A tied, high-severity mdb-debarment flag (category 'sanctions') sorted below a medium resignation. FLAG_WEIGHTS has no bar, debar or sanction terms, the category fallback covers only 'regulatory', and severity is never compared when sorting red flags.

title: Coverage text contradicts the screens: Delaware 'not covered' after it ran; partial sources unmentioned
scenario: In r9, delaware-courts answered 3 lookups (clear), yet notCovered says 'Court dockets (CourtListener is not enabled...), including US state courts and the Delaware Court of Chancery'. us-agency-orders, federal-register and us-lobbying show 'partial' in screens, but partlyAnswered ignores s.partial, so the brief's gaps section is silent about them. Web archive's 3 failed lookups out of 25 are not mentioned either.
fix: Drop the Delaware clause when delaware-courts answered. Include sources with s.partial in partlyAnswered (reason: 'parts did not answer: ...'). List every failed lookup count under 20% as a one-line note, not nothing.
evidence: Jest repro and r9 brief: the notCovered[0] string, and screens us-agency-orders 'partial' absent from GAPS.
verifyNote: notCoveredFor adds the Delaware Court of Chancery clause whenever court-dockets is silent, without checking delaware-courts. partlyAnswered checks only errors at 20% or more and waitedOut, never s.partial; my run showed uk-gazette 'partial' missing from partlyAnswered. Failed lookups under 20% never reach the brief.
betterFix: Also add s.partial and failures under 20% to coverage.searched rows, so that cleanScreens and the brief read one source of truth.

title: Name-only noise is numbered ahead of every record about the person
scenario: score() weighs severity x3 over match x2, so a possible medium item (9) outranks a confirmed info one (7). In r9, #2-#7 are the RAMP & CO LTD liquidation, 'Body found near ... Boat Ramp', and 'The Ramp church ... abused two minors', all ahead of #9 onward. Hacker News 'Ramp-Up' (#134-#136), placeholder text (r8 #37/#38) and a people-search-style bio site (#137) are kept too.
fix: Rank tied records first: sort by match tier (confirmed/likely, company, possible), then score. Drop records with data.companyNamesake that name neither the person nor the company as a name. Drop pages whose snippet advertises age, net worth or marital status (people-search style), and template placeholder text.
evidence: Jest repro: four possible records numbered 1-5 before the confirmed one. r9 sources #5 and #7.
verifyNote: score() gives severity x3 against match x2: a possible medium press record scores 6+2+1=9 and a confirmed info one 0+6+1=7, so name-only noise is numbered first. Sorting by match tier first is consistent with rule 2. Dropping people-search pages is consistent with the privacy rule, though those hosts should already be blocked in guardrails.
betterFix: Sort tied records (confirmed, likely, company) before possible ones, then by score. Do not drop companyNamesake records outright. Move them to a collapsed 'name only' group at the end, which keeps coverage honest.

title: One page is counted 3-11 times, which inflates totals; archived copies and own posts lose their tie
scenario: r8: merge.dev is #3/#13/#20, forbes #5/#6/#16/#21, accel #10/#15/#22, plus #37/#38 graded possible. The substack page is #14/#26. The bottom line says '26 tied' but there are about 10 pages. r9 has 11 copies of the Fortune pieces, and 'Gil Feig' lists 13 records. Her own post x.com/shensi/status/... (#44) is 'possible'.
fix: Canonicalise URLs: strip the web.archive.org prefix and www, resolve page-reader and search duplicates. Group them as one record with alsoIn, and give the group its strongest tie. A URL under a trusted profile URL (x.com/shensi/...) is at least likely. Count totals per page.
evidence: r8 sections archive, career, press and identity listings; r8 #44 url https://x.com/shensi/status/2123466322440818768 has match possible.
verifyNote: In deepCheck, pageKey is urlKey plus the headline of the title, so one URL found under different titles (search result vs page reader) is kept twice. urlKey does not strip the web.archive.org/web/<ts>/ prefix, and archive records are exempt from URL dedupe. The report adds no URL grouping. I did not check the r8/r9 counts.
betterFix: Fix this mainly in deepCheck.js: drop the title from pageKey for non-archive records, unwrap archive replay URLs in urlKey, and merge copies into alsoIn while keeping the strongest match (upgradeKept). In the report, count totals per canonical page. Raise a URL under a trusted profile URL to likely only if it is the same platform handle and the record names the person.

title: Timeline is archive capture dates and a 1994 domain; real career events are missing
scenario: In r9, 39 of 47 timeline rows are 'page as of' or 'archived N times' captures, and the first event is 'ramp.com: registered 1994-03-14' (a domain bought later). Paribus founded 2014, acquired by Capital One 2016, Ramp founded March 2019 and Harvard 2012 are absent. In r8, 8 of 9 rows are captures.
fix: Exclude archive snapshot and summary records (data.kind !== 'change') from the timeline. Put a domain registered before the company's founding year as 'domain first registered (earlier owner)', off the timeline and out of WHAT CHECKS OUT. Add dated events read from tied quotes (founded/joined/graduated/acquired + year) with their cites.
evidence: r9 timeline dump: 1994-03-14 n=103 first, followed mostly by archive rows.
verifyNote: The `rest` filter includes category 'archive' with no data.kind check, so 'snapshot' capture records fill the timeline. domains.js gives the corporate record the registration date as its date, so a 1994 domain registration becomes the first event. No code reads dated career events from tied quotes.

title: One liquidation is shown as three 'possible namesake' matters
scenario: In r9, the UK Gazette notices #2, #3 and #4 (Appointment of Liquidators, Notices to Creditors, Resolutions for Winding-up) for RAMP & CO LTD on 2024-07-23 are three entries under 'Possible namesakes' and three 'Rule out' bullets in the brief. Name-only grouping needs 2 shared headline words and Jaccard 0.4, and these headlines share none.
fix: In matterKey, group register and gazette records by the legal company name in the record plus the date (or within 14 days), before headline matching. Use the notice company from the title or quote, normalised.
evidence: r9 possibleNamesake list: n=2, 3, 4, each with more=[].
verifyNote: For 'possible' records, matterKey and agreement need at least 2 shared headline words and Jaccard 0.4. Event words such as liquidat and winding-up, and the company name in `skip`, are removed, so three notices about one company on one date stay separate. This is cosmetic: they stay with the possible namesakes either way.
betterFix: For uk-gazette and fr-bodacc, key the matter on the notice's company name (from data, or title or quote) plus a date within 14 days, before headline matching.

title: Real company news demoted to 'not clearly this company'
scenario: In r9, #6 'After a failed partnership, Ramp's backers lobbied Washington to probe rival Airwallex's China ties' (Dealroom, The Information) is about Ramp. BUSINESS lacks backers, rival, partnership, lobbied and fintech-peer words, so ordinaryWordOnly marks it possible and it lands with the possible namesakes.
fix: Widen BUSINESS (backers, rival, partnership, lobby*, competitor, deal, acquisition, payments, card, expense, Series, round). Treat the possessive or capitalised company word followed by a business noun as a name. Also accept a known peer company name (from tied records) in the same text.
evidence: r9 #6 matchReasons: 'the word "Ramp" appears, but not clearly as this company'. Jest repro reproduced match=possible.
verifyNote: BUSINESS lacks backers, rival, partnership, lobbying and competitor, so a headline about Ramp's backers fails BUSINESS.test unless the quote has a listed word, and is marked as a companyNamesake. Widening the list is safe because PART_OF_LONGER still catches 'boat ramp' and 'The Ramp church'.
betterFix: Widen BUSINESS, but keep 'deal', 'card' and 'payments' out unless next to the company word: they are common in unrelated news. Treating the possessive form ('Ramp's') followed by a business noun as a name is a good signal.

title: Caps cut records without telling the reader
scenario: The timeline slices at 60, capWikiOther drops articles from the report and its totals, and the quoted brief keeps 14 red flags, 8 company matters, 10 checks, 10 claim changes, 10 related parties, 8 namesakes and 5 possible changes. writeDeepBrief sends 12 company matters. None of these says how many were left out, so a 15th red flag disappears from the brief.
fix: Return omitted counts (timelineOmitted, wikiOtherDropped) in the report. In quotedDeepBrief, append '… and N more [see report]' after every slice. Tell the model 'N more company matters not shown'.
evidence: report.js lines 159, 627, 794 and 803-808 use slice() with no remainder text.
verifyNote: These slices are visible in the code: slice(0,14) red flags, 8 company matters, 10 checks, 10 claim changes, 10 related parties, 8 and 5 in the gaps section, timeline 60, capWikiOther, and 12 company matters sent to the model. None reports how many were left out. Saying so is required by the honest-coverage rule (rule 5).

title: When no record ties the person to the typed company, the report does not say so: a thin footprint reads as clean
scenario: A person with almost no web presence, or one falsely claiming to run the company, yields 0 confirmed or likely records. The header shows a green '0 tied to this person' chip and a green '0 red flags' chip, and the brief says 'No serious record is tied to this person'. Nothing states that the claimed role or company could not be confirmed by any independent record, which is itself a diligence signal. Every watchlist or court hit stays 'possible'.
evidence: state.identity.note is set only in resolveIdentity (inferred or ambiguous, when no company was given). With a typed company, status is 'given' and no note is ever written. DeepCheck.js gives '{confirmed+likely} tied' a chip-good class unconditionally.
fix: When a company was typed and no confirmed record names the person with it, add an identity note ('No independent record ties NAME to COMPANY; verify identity and role directly'). Put it in the brief and the gaps list, and make the chips neutral or amber rather than green.
